title: Vision and the eye
purpose: Trace the light route. Distinguish the iris from the pupil.
fallback: Light passes through the cornea, aqueous humour, pupil, lens and vitreous humour to reach the retina.

title: Eye anatomy recap
purpose: Track how the ciliary muscle, ligaments and lens change for a near object.
fallback: For near vision, ciliary muscles contract, ligament tension decreases and the lens becomes rounder.

title: Rods and visual pigments
purpose: Identify the role of rods in dim light, without treating rods as the optic nerve.
fallback: Rhodopsin contains opsin and retinal. Photoreceptors change transmitter release; ganglion-cell axons carry action potentials toward the brain.

title: Hearing: from sound to a signal
purpose: Name the point where mechanical movement is converted into an electrical response.
fallback: The tympanum and ossicles conduct vibration. Fluid and basilar-membrane movement bend cochlear hair cells, which influence auditory neurons.

title: The hearing pathway
purpose: Follow the sequence from the outer ear into the cochlea.
fallback: The pinna and auditory canal collect sound; the tympanum, ossicles and oval window transmit its energy toward cochlear fluid.

title: Pitch and loudness
purpose: Distinguish pitch from loudness using the stimulus rather than everyday labels.
fallback: Pitch relates to frequency; loudness relates to intensity. Different basilar-membrane regions respond most strongly to different frequencies.

title: Hearing loss and the sensory pathway
purpose: Separate a sound-conduction problem from a receptor or neural problem.
fallback: Conductive hearing impairment affects sound transmission in the outer or middle ear. Sensorineural impairment affects receptor or neural function.

title: Balance and head movement
purpose: Compare the stimulus for semicircular canals with the stimulus for the utricle and saccule.
fallback: Semicircular canals respond to changes in rotation. Weighted otolithic membranes in the utricle and saccule respond to linear acceleration and head tilt.
